bullets.title: 10yr yield at 5.28-5.34% — macro regime still Normal expansion, but rate hike odds and curve shape are key risks
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury hit 5.34% intraday (highest since 2002), up 53bps in September, yet 22V's macro regime model shows 70% probability of remaining in Normal expansion over 6 months with only 10% one-year recession risk. October FOMC hike odds fell to 37-38% post-PCE but Wolfe still models two more hikes (Oct/Dec); 22V survey shows 65% of investors see 6% as the level that breaks equities, with 5.5% already a headwind for 32%. Yield curve flattening is weighing on Financials, Gold, and Silver per Hedgeye.

bullets.title: September ISM Manufacturing 54.5 miss; prices paid surge to 77.9 — all 16 industries paying more
bullets.body: September ISM Manufacturing came in at 54.5 vs. consensus 55.0, with prices paid jumping 6.8pts to 77.9 (vs. 73.0 expected); all 16 industries and 24 commodities reported rising input costs, with zero declines. Supplier delivery times are lengthening due to energy costs, Canada tariffs, and AI infrastructure demand straining domestic steel capacity. Production growth slowed slightly while new orders and employment ticked higher.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Q4 2026 macro: Quad 2 (growth + inflation accelerating), dollar up, stay long tech/short cyclicals
bullets.body: Hedgeye frames Q4 as Quad 2 — growth and inflation both accelerating on easy comps, tax stimulus, tariff refunds, and peak AI capex returns — with household net wealth up $21T TTM. The 2-year yield is making new cycle highs as markets price ongoing Fed tightening rather than a hold/ease pivot; USD breakout is the central signal, positively correlated with Bitcoin and U.S. equity growth factors. Portfolio expression: long XLK, IGV, BUG, XLV; short XLF (-7.5% Sep), XLY (-6.7%), XLU (-6.6%), XLI (-4.7%).

bullets.title: AI broadening thesis: leadership shifting from infra to software/adopters, but buildout far from over
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes AI leadership is broadening toward Software Enablers and Adopters (improving earnings visibility, lower valuations) while infrastructure, semis, and power bottleneck plays retain long-run upside; US data center power demand is projected to reach 97GW by 2028 with a potential 57GW supply shortfall. Hedgeye flags that 15 of 35 AI names are already in Bearish TREND and all 'Power Grid' infrastructure names have broken down, while the 'Cash Funded Four' are up +17% in 60 days vs. Neoclouds -7%. GS September sentiment highlights the 'inference economy' and capex/asset-light AI strategies gaining traction.

bullets.title: Agentic AI disruption framework: who wins and who gets disintermediated
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's agentic AI basket (MSXXCLAW) is up +22% since META's Muse launch while the at-risk basket (MSXXARSK) is down 9%. Winners named include SHOP (agentic storefronts), TWLO (incremental messaging/voice from agents), and NVDA (infrastructure). At-risk: OTAs (EXPE, BKNG, ABNB face booking displacement), auto retail, subscription services, and cable/telecoms (agents helping customers switch or downgrade). Digital advertising faces open-web human traffic deceleration.

bullets.title: September global tech performance: Mag7 +4.2%, Semis +9.3%, Memory +10.4%; Software lagged
bullets.body: Per JPM's September recap, tech strength persisted but leadership dispersed within themes (Semis vs. Software) rather than across sectors. Global rates sold off sharply on 'higher-for-longer/structurally higher real rates' narrative; USD positioning turned constructive vs. low-yielders. European equities underperformed (SXXP -2.5%, France -4.4% on fiscal/political concerns); Brent rallied above $100 on Middle East re-escalation.

bullets.title: Taiwan and Korea PMIs at cycle highs in September, signaling strong AI-driven export demand
bullets.body: Taiwan's manufacturing PMI surged +2.0pts to a cycle-high 56.7% (exports component 57.6%), which leads US ISM by one month with 70% correlation. Korea's PMI jumped +1.6pts to 53.9% with exports hitting a 25-year high; September nominal exports reached a record $111B (+83.5% YoY vs. 62.5% consensus), with tech exports up 263% YoY driven by AI capex. Piper Sandler's model forecasts the Foreign Mfg PMI cooling to 50.4% by August 2027 as higher rates and oil weigh.

bullets.title: Friday payrolls setup: investors lean risk-on; 90k consensus, >120k would be risk-off
bullets.body: 22V survey shows 53% of investors expect Friday labor data to be mixed/negligible, 41% risk-on, with only 6% expecting risk-off — the lowest risk-off share since December 2025. Survey payroll consensus is 90k (in line with Bloomberg) with a right tail toward 130k; payrolls above 120k are seen as risk-off (inflationary signal), 100-120k risk-on. AHE expected in-line at 0.3%; a 4.1% unemployment rate is seen as risk-on while 4.0% is risk-off.

bullets.title: US midterms: >90% Dem House, >60% Dem Senate per prediction markets; AI data center states shrinking
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs notes prediction markets imply >90% probability Democrats net at least 3 House seats and >60% chance they flip the Senate. 22V flags that AI data center 'builder-friendly' states are dropping from 27 to ~15 post-midterms, with Texas (35% of US capacity) as the linchpin; TCEQ air permit delays and ERCOT queue reviews are already pausing approvals, which will keep compute prices elevated.

bullets.title: Market breadth extremely narrow: only 40.6% of S&P above 200-DMA; 77% of stocks declining
bullets.body: The McClellan Summation Index is at its lowest since November 2023, with only 40.6% of S&P 500 constituents above their 200-day moving averages. Hedgeye notes that 77% of stocks are declining despite S&P 500 headline strength, and the gap between SPX and the average stock's 52-week high is -17.05%, the largest since September 2020. 19 stocks hit 52-week highs vs. 246 at 52-week lows; Finance sector dominated the lows (82 total).

bullets.title: ACN +18% on broad beat and FY27 guidance; AI demand broadening from experimentation into enterprise
bullets.body: Accenture Q4 revenue of $18.68B beat its own guidance range; FY27 local currency growth guided at +3-6% vs. Street's +1-4%. AI+data bookings grew 3x (revenue 2x) vs. 2025, with 141 quarterly client bookings above $100M. Management noted AI demand is broadening from experimentation into enterprise transformation, with most clients still in foundational stages; Managed Services increasingly used as a transformation vehicle blending consulting and AI.

bullets.title: Geopolitical tail risks elevated: Hormuz stalemate, Russia-NATO tensions, Brent above $100
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags a stalemate in the Strait of Hormuz one month before US midterms, growing Russian hostilities toward NATO countries, and defense spending under review on Capitol Hill. JPM's September recap notes energy markets rallied with Brent above $100 on Middle East re-escalation, while the OAT-Bund spread reached levels not seen since 2002 amid French fiscal credibility concerns and a €54B deficit reduction effort.

bullets.title: Equity positioning/leverage back near YTD highs — Q4 deleveraging risk rising
bullets.body: JPM notes leveraged equity ETF AUM-to-market-cap ratios are rising again (~70% of the April-June range) and equity positioning/leverage has re-emerged near YTD highs, representing a potential Q4 headwind. Retail flows were weak at the 12th percentile in September (weakest since December 2024) with record rotation into long-end Treasury ETFs (TLT +6.1 z-score). Russell 2000 median short interest is at the 99.8th percentile.

bullets.title: S&P Utilities +6.1% in September on data center power demand; nuclear/fuel cell contracts validating sector
bullets.body: The S&P 500 Utilities Index outperformed the broad market significantly (+6.1% vs. +0.5%) driven by AI data center power demand. Bloom Energy surged on a $6.4B Brookfield fuel-cell JV for data centers; Constellation signed a 20-year, 190MW nuclear PPA with Amazon; GE Vernova is targeting a $200B order backlog by early 2027. Texas halted new data center permits pending a grid audit, and California signed a new oversight bill, adding regulatory complexity.

bullets.title: Alts flow deterioration accelerating: wealth-channel flows down 35% YoY; private credit near zero
bullets.body: JPM reports July wealth-channel alternative flows collapsed to $5.4B (down 35% YoY vs. $8.2B average); private credit flows fell to ~$400M from a $5.0B peak. Rotation thesis is failing — capital leaving credit is not flowing into real estate/PE/infra. August data was soft across Blackstone, Apollo, Ares, and Blue Owl, with Carlyle showing negative net sales. Infrastructure is the only bright spot, driven by compute/AI demand.

bullets.title: Fed inflation: Core PCE slightly warm on revisions; Minneapolis Fed Kashkari says inflation still too high
bullets.body: Kashkari asserted inflation remains too high despite a slightly better-than-expected August Core PCE headline print; revision surprises were steeper than expected and Market Price Only figures came in warm. One analyst estimates inflation is 50bps too high when excluding transitory items. The productivity-growth revision (nonfarm business productivity trend now ~2.8%) could provide a disinflationary offset if the Fed chooses to look through it.

bullets.title: FCC likely to restrict China optical transceivers at 3.2T gen (~2028); COHR/LITE benefit on laser share
bullets.body: FCC's Covered List is emerging as the near-term mechanism to restrict Chinese-built optical transceivers, expected to phase in at the 3.2T generation (2028-2029 ramp). Chinese transceivers remain importable if 65% of BOM is US-sourced (DSP/laser), making laser pricing and COHR/LITE component share the stronger read-through. US transceiver capacity is ~8x smaller than combined Chinese capacity, requiring a multi-year build to replace volumes.

bullets.title: Macau September GGR -1% YoY at 82% of 2019 levels; JPM cuts Q4 outlook to -6% YoY
bullets.body: Macau September GGR of MOP 18.1B was the weakest daily rate since September 2024, with VIP down ~10% YoY at just 46% of 2019 levels while mass/slot grew +2% YoY. JPM cut FY26E industry GGR to MOP 249B (+1% YoY, 85% of 2019) and revised Q4 down to -6% YoY (from -1%), citing possible China tax crackdown, seasonality ahead of Golden Week, and macro weakness.

bullets.title: GOOGL antitrust: dismissal win in Chegg/Penske suits; ad-tech trial path cleared for TDAY
bullets.body: A US District Court dismissed all antitrust claims from Chegg and Penske Media against Google, ruling that expectation of traffic is not an agreement and that Search and AI Overviews are not separate products. In contrast, USA TODAY (TDAY) surged +14% after the court denied most of Google's summary judgment motions in the separate ad-tech MDL, clearing the path to trial over alleged monopolization of digital advertising technology.

bullets.title: Digital assets institutionalizing rapidly; Morgan Stanley rolling out new client products
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's roundtable highlighted digital assets' multi-trillion-dollar market cap and accelerating institutionalization, with the firm rolling out new portfolio-access products. Tokenization of real-world assets is described as occurring today, not a future concept. Three investor archetypes are emerging: digital gold (Bitcoin), venture-style growth, and portfolio diversifiers; 24/7 trading capability is seen as a key adoption driver for corporates and investors.
